display.purpose: The product name in the header strip. One per page.

figure.purpose: A printed number — bank, team value, points, entry number. Always sits under a head.

head.purpose: Column heads, section heads, the bench band, and run-in labels like After / Marked.

tab.purpose: Tab bar, text buttons, the stub action, the stamp.

row.purpose: Condensed tabular row text in the table of the fifteen.

body.purpose: Checklist labels and prose, set at text width. Capped at 60ch.

pinned.purpose: When a figure was true, or the caveat under an action. Never larger.

motion.name: biro-draw
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: the biro X is drawn onto a marked coupon box, not switched on. Guarded by prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: ink-shift
motion.purpose: Every other state change: tab colour and underline, box hover wash, stub and text-button hover. Colour only, never transform.

narrative.overview:
The site is this week's football pools coupon: a sheet of warm paper, set in black print ink, ruled with hairlines, numbered down the left, with boxes you mark in biro and a stub you hand in. One spot colour — coupon blue — is what the printer had on the press that week, so it appears on the header strip, the stub button, the open tab, the filled tally cells and the pitch drawing, and nowhere else. Red is not a palette colour; it is the rubber stamp the clerk banged on the sheet, and it says two things only: when the coupon closes, and who cannot play.

Density is printed density, not app density. Hairline rules do all the work that a card and a shadow would do elsewhere: a rule-strong line under a section head, a rule line under every coupon row, a dashed tear line above the stub. There is no elevation anywhere on the page, no gradient fill, no rounded container, no shadow. A figure never floats; it sits in a column under a printed head with its moment pinned underneath it ("As of run 12 Sept 04:11 UTC").

The world is deliberately the opposite of the category. FPL tools are dark pitches of shirt badges over neon stat cards; this is a paper document that tells you what to do, shows you what it read, and admits what it does not know. Nothing on the page is predicted; every number is a thing that was true at a stated time.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, black print ink, no dark mode.
One spot colour, used structurally, never decoratively.
Biro blue for everything the user marks; red for the stamp only.
One variable type family, printed condensed (78% width) or set at text width (100%), on a fixed rem scale.
Zero radius, zero shadow, zero gradient fill. Hairline rules instead.
Tabular numerals everywhere; every figure pinned to its moment.

rules.name: The Who-Printed-It Rule
rules.body: Spot blue is the printer's; biro blue is the user's. A colour choice is settled by asking who put the mark on the paper. A checkbox X is biro. A filled tally cell is spot, because the coupon was printed with those backers already counted.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Red appears only on the closing stamp and on a player who cannot play. It never marks a falling price, a warning, a low score, or a destructive button. A price change prints in soft ink and lets the sign (+ / −) carry the direction.

rules.name: The No-Grey Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is mixed from ink and paper, so the page stays warm. Never introduce a pure grey, a pure white, or a pure black.

rules.name: The Two-Widths Rule
rules.body: If it is printed on the coupon — a head, a row, a figure, a button — it is condensed at 78%. If it is something to read — a sentence, a detail, a caveat — it is at 100%. Nothing else on the width axis.

rules.name: The Pinned Figure Rule
rules.body: No figure appears without its moment. Every number either carries a pinned note under it or sits in a block whose pinned line states the run time and prices-as-of. Nothing predicted is printed at all.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Tabular numerals are on globally. Do not turn them off for "nicer" proportional figures; the coupon's columns must align down the page.

rules.name: The One Sheet Rule
rules.body: The page is one document, not a stack of panels. Do not introduce a second scroll container, a sidebar that scrolls independently, or a sticky footer bar. The only sticky element in the system is the desktop column head.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs to feel separate, give it a rule or a second-stock band. Never a shadow, never a border-radius, never a gradient fill.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius is 0 everywhere. The only exception is a printed circled letter (the C/V marks and the pitch discs). If a new component wants a rounded corner, it wants to be a different product.

dos: Do print anything structural — head, row, figure, button, tab — in condensed setting (wdth 78%) and anything readable at text width (100%).
Do give every figure a head above it and a pinned note beneath it stating when it was true.
Do separate with a rule: hairline between peers, heavy rule between sections, 2px dashed for a tear line.
Do use spot blue for what the printer set (strip, open tab, stub, tally fills, pitch lines, links) and biro blue for what the user marks.
Do keep red for the closing stamp and for a player who cannot play, and let a sign (+ / −) carry direction everywhere else.
Do build new tabs from the existing vocabulary — head, figure, pinned, rule-b / rule-strong-b, coupon rows, tally, box, textbtn, unprinted — before inventing a class.
Do inline any icon as SVG from lucide-react at 16px with strokeWidth 2.25 and aria-hidden, and only where a word cannot do the job.
Do label provisional, predicted or untimed data as such, and print nothing predicted at all.
Do guard any motion with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, resolving to the finished state.
donts: Don't add a shadow, an elevation, a glow, or a "lifted" hover. There are none in the system.
Don't add a border-radius. Zero everywhere; the circled C/V mark and the pitch discs are the only circles.
Don't use a gradient as a fill, a background, or an accent. The one gradient in the build is a mask on the phone tab row that fades the scroll edge; that is a mask, not a surface.
Don't wrap content in a card. A section is a head, a rule, and rows.
Don't introduce a second accent colour, a chart palette, a success green, or a warning amber. The palette is closed.
Don't colour a price change, a delta or a score red or green.
Don't use pure white, pure black or a neutral grey.
Don't add a second type family, a second axis, a fluid/clamped size, or a size outside the seven-step rem scale.
Don't use an icon font, an emoji or a glyph character as an icon, and don't put an icon where a printed word works.
Don't write a kicker or eyebrow above a heading. Labels are printed column heads above a value or run-in before a line; they are never a decorative tag over a title.
Don't animate anything but the biro X. No page transitions, no fades on mount, no skeleton shimmer, no number count-ups; state changes are 150ms ease-out on colour only.
Don't add a dark mode. The world is a sheet of paper.
